thread:
sarah_acme: Hey team — running into a weird problem after switching to the quantized model. Our embeddings responses sometimes come back with length 384 instead of 1536. Only happens when we send multiple inputs in a single request. Any ideas? :confused:

maya_support: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you share the exact API call (sanitized) and which model tag you used? Also are you using our official SDK or raw HTTP?

sarah_acme: Sent via direct curl from our service (redacted):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\  
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' \\  
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  
  -d '{"model":"openembed-v2-int8","input":["alpha","beta","gamma","delta"],"batch_size":4}'
```
Response sample (trimmed):
```
{"data":[{"index":0,"embedding":[/* 384 floats */]}, ...]}
```
If we set batch_size to 1 we get 1536 floats per embedding. This started after we moved to openembed-v2-int8 to reduce cost. We're on SDK v0.9.2 in prod but tried curl above outside the SDK.

arjun_ml: Thanks for the reproduction steps. I pulled your curl into a local test against the exact model tag and I can reproduce. Multi-input requests produce 384-dim outputs; single-inputs are 1536. Looks like a bug in the quantized multi-batch output path (maybe pooling or reshape logic). I’ll add logs to the runner.

arjun_ml: Extract from the model runner log when processing the batched request:
```
[2026-03-15T20:12:03Z] model_tag=openembed-v2-int8 batch=4 seq_len=32 dtype=int8 op=quantized_forward
[2026-03-15T20:12:03Z] kernel=packed_matmul pack_factor=4 expected_output_dim=1536 observed_output_dim=384
[2026-03-15T20:12:03Z] postprocess=embedding_pooling mode=none
```

maya_support: That observed_output_dim explains the truncated vectors. Ethan — did infra roll any batching/packing improvements around 03/14-03/15 that could affect int8 paths?

ethan_infra: We deployed runtime change runtime/v2.14 on 2026-03-14 to improve memory usage for int8 workloads (packing changes). It targeted memory layout only but might have touched pack_factor. I'm marking canary and checking metrics.

deploy-bot: runtime/v2.14 deployed canary us-east-1 at 2026-03-14T22:40:00Z :white_check_mark:

arjun_ml: Minimal repro steps I used:
1) Pull model openembed-v2-int8 to test cluster
2) Run the curl with batch_size=4 and capture full JSON
3) Run compare script to check dims:
```
python tools/check_embed_dims.py before.json after.json
```
Output:
```
expected_dim: 1536
observed_dim: 384
count_mismatch: 4
```

maya_support: For an immediate workaround for customers — please use the fp16 variant (openembed-v2-fp16) or set batch_size to 1. We'll mark this as high priority.

sarah_acme: Ok we'll try fp16 for now. Curious about quality tradeoffs between int8 and fp16 for embeddings — will this change similarity/nearest-neighbor results much?

arjun_ml: Short answer: int8 can shift embeddings and occasionally reduce cosine similarity for near neighbors; fp16 is closer to the full-precision baseline. However, the main issue here is wrong dimensionality for batched int8, which invalidates comparisons entirely. We'll run a small eval on a sample of your queries and post delta metrics.

arjun_ml: Preliminary evaluation on a 500-sample set:
```
N=500
avg_cosine_fp16=0.944
avg_cosine_int8_batch1=0.935
avg_cosine_int8_batch4=0.786  # obviously bad, dims mismatch
```
Note: int8 batch1 shows a small fidelity drop vs fp16; expected. Batch4 drop is due to the dimension bug.

ethan_infra: I'm snapshotting canary logs and checking whether rollback to runtime/v2.13 eliminates the issue. If yes, we'll either rollback canary or patch the pack factor handling.

arjun_ml: Created internal ticket ML-8001: "quantized output reshape bug when batch>1" and linked logs and minimal repro. Proposed fixes:
- Fix reshape/pack factor computation in quantized forward (preferred)
- As a temporary internal workaround, add a runtime flag REDWOOD_FORCE_OUT_DIM to pad/reshape outputs to expected dim (experimental)

maya_support: Support action items:
- Notify affected customers with recommended workarounds (use fp16 or batch_size=1) — maya_support
- Keep this thread updated until fix is released — maya_support

sarah_acme: Thanks everyone. We'll switch to fp16 for now and report if we see quality issues. Please share ETA when available.

arjun_ml: Rough ETA: patch and canary in ~36-48 hours after root-cause confirmation, then progressive rollout if canary metrics look good. I'll post the PR and link here.

maya_support: Marking this SR P1 due to customer impact on embeddings. CC'ing Sarah on follow-ups.

arjun_ml: One more note for engineers: int8 packing assumed contiguous embedding chunks per sample; the batched packer introduced a pack_factor bug that divided output channels by 4 when pack_factor!=1. Fix will ensure output_dim = base_dim * pack_factor when computing final shape.

sarah_acme: Appreciate the fast response. Please keep us in the loop and thanks for the workaround suggestions. :pray:
